transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-08-13
- Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Linh (CSM), Elena (HarborMark Head of Platform), Jon (Infra Lead), Priya (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
HarborMark is up for renewal in ~6 weeks. They're evaluating a capacity uplift plus adding EU and APAC regions (data residency constraints in EU). Main concerns: 95th pct latency SLA <200ms for customer-facing endpoints, cost per token vs preferred batching, and private VPC option for regulated data. Next steps: Redwood to provide updated pricing scenarios, SOC2/SAML docs; HarborMark to provide workload samples; run EU benchmark.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity uplift sizing, multi-region (EU/AU/APAC) onboarding, private VPC vs hosted fallback, compliance (SOC2/KMS), benchmark plan, procurement timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, is the time still good?
[00:03] Elena: yep, all good from HarborMark, thanks Maya.
[00:07] Maya: cool quick roundtable then we'll go into the renewal numbers and the region plan. Ravi's here to talk throughput and latency testing.
[00:13] Ravi: hey all, hi.
[00:14] Jon: morning.
[00:16] Priya: hi.
[00:18] Maya: Elena, want to kick off with current state — what are you running today and what's changed since last quarter?
[00:24] Elena: sure. we're on Redwood hosted API, mainly text gen for support assistant and a reranker. currently peak is about 180 rps across embeddings + gen, 85 concurrent user requests in the evening surge. billing and usage have been steady but we've seen spikes due to a marketing event which is why we're looking at a capacity uplift. also compliance: a few enterprise customers in EU want their inference to stay in eu-west.
[00:45] Jon: to add, our infra is AWS, we have cross-account connectivity to Redwood Dedicated in us-west today; for EU we prefer either Redwood hosted eu region or a private VPC node in our eu account. latency target is tight — product wants 95th under 200ms for a 512 token average request.
[01:05] Ravi: okay that's helpful. quick clarifying q: when you say 512 avg, is that model tokens or prompt+completion?
[01:11] Elena: combined, so prompt + completion, typically prompt is 120 tokens, completion average 392.
[01:17] Ravi: got it. that matters for batching profile and kv cache sizing.
[01:20] Maya: timeline wise Priya, you mentioned procurement windows — when do you need final commercial terms?
[01:24] Priya: decision by end of September ideally — renewal at start of October. procurement will need standard contract language and SOC2, plus an SLA addendum if possible.
[01:32] Maya: perfect, we'll prioritize that. Linh will circulate SOC2 and SSO docs.
[01:36] Linh: yep I'll upload the docs after this call.
[01:38] Jon: on region choices, can you outline the difference between Redwood Hosted eu region vs Dedicated in our VPC? performance, cost, and data flow are the main dimensions.
[01:47] Ravi: high level: hosted eu is fastest to enable — we have pre-placed capacity and you call our eu endpoint — but it's multi-tenant and uses Redwood-managed keys by default. Dedicated VPC gives you isolation and control (bring-your-own-kms) but adds provisioning lead time and higher committed costs. for latency, both can meet your 95th under 200ms with correct sizing; Dedicated sometimes has marginally higher cold-starts during scale events, but it's tunable.
[02:14] Elena: what's the typical provisioning lead time for a private VPC node?
[02:18] Maya: for EU private it can be 6-8 weeks depending on capacity, sometimes 4 if we have spare onprem-equivalent nodes, but plan for 6.
[02:26] Jon: hmm that pushes us close to procurement window. Is there a hybrid — start hosted eu then flip to VPC?
[02:31] Ravi: yes that's our recommended path for customers on tight timelines — start with hosted eu, run benchmarks, then transition to Dedicated VPC with a canary cutover. we support model pinning and routing policies so you can fallback to hosted if Dedicated has an incident.
[02:44] Elena: that fallback sounds good.
[02:46] Priya: cost — rough numbers please, we need a ballpark for budget planning.
[02:50] Maya: high level we ran three scenarios in the worksheet — continue current committed but add 2x capacity in us-west, add hosted eu region, or reserved Dedicated with VPC covering us-west+eu. i'll email the updated pricing after this call; scenario A (2x hosted) is lowest near-term cost, scenario C (Dedicated) gives predictable unit economics but higher commit.
[03:12] Jon: any changes in token pricing if we use larger batch sizes or quantized models?
[03:16] Ravi: token pricing from Redwood is usage-based but effective unit cost improves with batching + kv cache. plus we can recommend quantization (8-bit) for some variants — quality tradeoffs depend on your eval set. we'll include model and quant recommendations in the doc.
[03:30] Elena: about quality — last time we saw a small regression when you recommended a 4-bit profile, we had an eval failure. how do you handle regression detection for rollouts?
[03:38] Linh: we have pre-deploy evaluation hooks and can tie regressions to alerting; our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization only after comparing to baseline prompts. for enterprise customers we can run those evals with your test prompts.
[03:49] Jon: can we run a local perf test in our eu account? we'd prefer to test egress and latencies from our VPC.
[03:55] Ravi: yes — for Dedicated we'll set up a test harness and give you temporary test endpoints in the eu stage. for hosted we can provide test keys to hit eu endpoints from your infra. either way we can script a 2-hour throughput test that matches your qps and seq distribution.
[04:07] Elena: great. what do you need from us to size the Dedicated node?
[04:11] Ravi: sample workload: qps profile, seq distribution, percent of streaming responses, and concurrency targets. plus any peak events. Jon can drop a CSV and we'll run the sizing calc.
[04:20] Jon: I'll export the traffic patterns — but note some endpoints call for simultaneous long-poll streaming for multi-turn chat, around 30 concurrent streams at peak.
[04:28] Ravi: okay include that, streaming affects memory and kv cache retention.
[04:31] Maya: switching to procurement — Priya, is there anything non-standard that will block sign-off?
[04:35] Priya: standard checks: indemnity, data processing addendum, and proof of encryption at rest + KMS control if we move to Dedicated. SOC2 is a checkbox but we also need a short runbook for incident response.
[04:46] Linh: incident response runbook is part of our enterprise pack — i'll include a redacted example. we also support ping-based monitoring and webhook tracing hooks.
[04:54] Elena: regarding data residency — storing logs in eu is critical. can Redwood keep audit logs in our eu datastore?
[05:00] Ravi: for Dedicated in your VPC, logs can be exported to your KMS and storage. for hosted eu, we retain logs in eu-managed storage for EU customers but certain telemetry may be routed to central ops; we'll mark that in the DPA.
[05:13] Jon: okay noted.
[05:15] Maya: let's talk benchmarks — propose we run a staged test: 1) baseline hosted eu test from your eu infra 2) throughput run with 2x expected peak 3) canary cutover trial to Dedicated (if you choose) — how long for each?
[05:28] Ravi: baseline is 1-2 hours to gather distributions; throughput run about 2 hours; canary depends on integration but we can do a morning cutover with rollback policy. total test window: ~1 day to get solid numbers.
[05:39] Jon: we can allocate a day next week.
[05:42] Priya: procurement timeline: we'll need final SOW and pricing by Aug 29 to reach legal and finance for end-of-September sign-off.
[05:51] Maya: we'll aim for 8/15 to share pricing and a tailored SOW.
[05:55] Elena: one other question — tokenization differences across model variants, do you see any variance that may affect cost? we've seen different token counts between models when switching.
[06:03] Ravi: yes tokenization varies by model family; the billing aligns to tokens emitted/processed so that's why getting a representative prompt set is important. we'll run tokenization counts on your prompts and show effective cost delta.
[06:14] Jon: competitive check — our platform team is also benchmarking OpenAI for gen quality and Lambda for hosting cost. what's Redwood's edge?
[06:21] Maya: our focus is production economics + operational controls: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, clear batching/cache levers that reduce real unit cost, and strong rollout tooling for regressions. we also provide first-class SLA and route-based tracing.
[06:34] Elena: fair.
[06:35] Priya: legal will ask about password rotation/KMS and SSO. do you support SCIM provisioning?
[06:40] Linh: yes SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, and we integrate with common IdPs; key rotation with BYOK is supported for Dedicated.
[06:47] Jon: are there any known gotchas when moving to eu region for models with stateful chat?
[06:52] Ravi: main items: kv cache latency if cross-region, and larger memory footprint for multi-turns. for that we size kv cache per-node and ensure co-location of user state. we'll document memory footprints for your average session length.
[07:03] Elena: thanks.
[07:05] Maya: quick recap before we close — action items and deadlines are in the next steps; we'll send pricing and SOC2 docs by Friday 8/15. Ravi will provision test keys and run EU throughput with the sample workload Jon provides; Linh will send technical SSO and incident runbook. anything else?
[07:22] Jon: just to confirm the benchmark will capture 95th pctl latency and also token throughput numbers, yes?
[07:26] Ravi: correct, we'll produce a short runbook and an output sheet with p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens/sec.
[07:32] Priya: legal will expect an SLA addendum; please include the temp remedy and credits.
[07:36] Maya: will do.
[07:38] Elena: perfect, thanks everyone.
[07:39] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and set a benchmark slot for next week.
[07:43] End of recording

Notes on transcription: occasional name mis-heard (HarborMark sometimes transcribed as Harbor Mark), product names may appear as "Redwood Dedicate" in parts of the audio, timestamps are aligned to speaker turns and not exact word-level timing.
